newsitem.title: USA: Arctic cold retreating, central U.S. to warm up.
newsitem.headline: Arctic cold retreating, central U.S. to warm up.

text.p: Arctic cold that blanketed the central United States and produced the coldest Christmas ever in Minneapolis will soon be replaced by warmer weather from the Dakotas to Texas, forecasters said.
Forecasters said the Arctic cold will retreat north into Canada by Friday allowing warmer air to spread over much of the Midwest.
Temperatures in Minneapolis on Christmas Day ranged from a low of -27 degrees Fahrenheit to a high of -9, said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather.
"Minneapolis had the coldest Christmas on record," Solberg said. The previous Christmas Day record was -6 in 1938.

Minneapolis residents continued to dig out from nearly three feet of snow. That area has received nearly double its normal amount of snowfall for the season-to-date, said the National Weather Service.
Early Thursday, sub-zero temperatures and six to 10 inches of snow on the ground slowed hog marketings from central Iowa and southern Minnesota, livestock dealers said.
"The big news is the Arctic air...looks like it may be retreating northward," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.

The warmup should begin Friday with temperatures in Iowa and northern Illinois rising to the mid 30s, and Missouri and southern Illinois to the low 40s. Highs in Kansas should reach the 50s early next week and in Texas the low 70s, he said.
A brief cold spell may occur Sunday in the upper U.S. Midwest, but should be quickly replaced by another warm system, said WSC's Burgio.
"There is nothing really serious about that," Burgio said of Sunday's cold system.
